```{r}
#imports and file load
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)

hybrids <- read.csv("../data/orchidroots_cattleya_hybrids.csv")
species <- read.csv("../data/orchidroots_cattleya_species.csv")

summary(hybrids)
summary(species)

```

```{r}
#Data Cleaning

# Remove subsp. and var. from Species entries 
species_filtered <- species[grepl("subsp\\. |\\svar\\.", species$Binomial) == FALSE, ]


# Remove any hybrids which are just synonyms 
hybrids_filtered <- hybrids[!grepl("Synonym of", hybrids$Parentage), ]

# Filter out the year 2025
hybrids_filtered <- hybrids_filtered[hybrids_filtered$Year != 2025, ]

#Move more data preparation here!
```

```{r}
#Examining Species acceptance status 
#Some species maybe not found in ncbi but probably still species
#Some recent classifications 

library(taxize)

# Function to check if species are accepted using NCBI (alternative database)
check_accepted_species_ncbi <- function(species_list) {
  accepted_species <- sapply(species_list, function(species) {
    # Get the taxonomic ID (taxid) from NCBI
    tax_info <- get_uid(species, db = "ncbi")
    
    # If a valid taxid (Taxonomic ID) is returned, it's accepted
    if (!is.na(tax_info)) {
      accepted <- TRUE
    } else {
      accepted <- FALSE
    }
    return(accepted)
  })
  return(accepted_species)
}

# Apply the function to the 'Binomial' column for NCBI
accepted_ncbi <- check_accepted_species_ncbi(species_filtered$Binomial)

# Add the results back to the data frame
species_filtered$Accepted <- accepted_ncbi

# Print the results for the whole dataset (showing species and their acceptance status)
print(species_filtered)

# Filter to get only accepted species
accepted_species_list <- species_filtered[species_filtered$Accepted == TRUE, ]
print("Accepted Species List:")
print(accepted_species_list)

# Filter to get only not accepted species
not_accepted_species_list <- species_filtered[species_filtered$Accepted == FALSE, ]
print("Not Accepted Species List:")
print(not_accepted_species_list)

```

```{r}
#exploratory plotting -- hybrids_filtered

#Distinguish Hybrid Type-----------------------------------------------------

# Function to classify hybrids_filtered based on capitalization of the second word
classify_hybrid <- function(parentage) {
  parents <- unlist(strsplit(as.character(parentage), " × "))  # Split parents
  
  is_species <- function(name) {
    words <- unlist(strsplit(name, " "))  # Split into words
    return(length(words) > 1 && grepl("^[a-z]", words[2]))  # Check if second word is lowercase
  }
  
  # Check if both parents are species
  if (all(sapply(parents, is_species))) {
    return("Primary Hybrid")
  } else {
    return("Complex Hybrid")
  }
}

# Apply classification to the dataset
hybrids_filtered$HybridType <- sapply(hybrids_filtered$Parentage, classify_hybrid)

#bar chart primary vs complex hybrids_filtered 
ggplot(hybrids_filtered, aes(x = hybrids_filtered$HybridType, fill = hybrids_filtered$HybridType)) +
  geom_bar() +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Primary vs. Complex hybrids_filtered", x = "Hybrid Type", y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal()

#hybrid type year by year ------------------------------------------------------
ggplot(hybrids_filtered, aes(x = hybrids_filtered$Year, fill = hybrids_filtered$HybridType)) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill") +  # Normalized by year

# Count hybrids_filtered by year and type
df_hybrid_trend <- as.data.frame(table(hybrids_filtered$Year, hybrids_filtered$HybridType))
colnames(df_hybrid_trend) <- c("Year", "HybridType", "Count")
df_hybrid_trend$Year <- as.numeric(as.character(df_hybrid_trend$Year))

# Plot trend count hybrid type over time
ggplot(df_hybrid_trend, aes(x = Year, y = Count, color = HybridType, group = HybridType)) +
  geom_line(size = 1) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(title = "Trend of Primary vs. Complex hybrids_filtered Over Time", x = "Year", y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal()

classify_hybrid <- function(parentage) {
  parents <- unlist(strsplit(as.character(parentage), " × "))  # Split parents
  
  is_hybrid <- function(name) {
    words <- unlist(strsplit(name, " "))  # Split name into words
    if (length(words) < 2) return(FALSE)  # Ensure there are at least two words
    return(grepl("^[A-Z]", words[2]))  # Check if the second word is capitalized
  }
  
  # Check classification based on capitalization
  if (all(sapply(parents, function(x) !is_hybrid(x)))) {
    return("Primary Hybrid")
  } else if (all(sapply(parents, function(x) is_hybrid(x)))) {
    return("Highly Complex Hybrid")
  } else {
    return("Complex Hybrid")
  }
}


# Apply classification to the dataset
hybrids_filtered$HybridType <- sapply(hybrids_filtered$Parentage, classify_hybrid)

# Bar chart primary vs complex vs highly complex
ggplot(hybrids_filtered, aes(x = HybridType, fill = HybridType)) +
  geom_bar() +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Primary vs. Complex vs. Highly Complex hybrids_filtered", x = "Hybrid Type", y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal()

# Hybrid type year by year
ggplot(hybrids_filtered, aes(x = Year, fill = HybridType)) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill") +  # Normalized by year
  labs(title = "Proportion of Primary vs. Complex vs. Highly Complex hybrids_filtered Over Time", x = "Year", y = "Proportion") +
  theme_minimal()

# Count hybrids by year and type
df_hybrid_trend <- as.data.frame(table(hybrids_filtered$Year, hybrids_filtered$HybridType))
colnames(df_hybrid_trend) <- c("Year", "HybridType", "Count")
df_hybrid_trend$Year <- as.numeric(as.character(df_hybrid_trend$Year))

# Plot trend count hybrid type over time
ggplot(df_hybrid_trend, aes(x = Year, y = Count, color = HybridType, group = HybridType)) +
  geom_line(size = 1) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(title = "Trend of Primary vs. Complex vs. Highly Complex hybrids_filtered Over Time", x = "Year", y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal()


# Create a data frame for the corsage era rectangle
corsage_era <- data.frame(
  xmin = 1920,
  xmax = 1950,
  ymin = -Inf,
  ymax = Inf,
  era = "Cattleya Corsage Era"
)

ggplot() +
  # Draw the corsage era shaded background with legend
  geom_rect(data = corsage_era, 
            aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax, fill = era),
            alpha = 0.2, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  # Plot the hybrid trend lines
  geom_line(data = df_hybrid_trend, 
            aes(x = Year, y = Count, color = HybridType, group = HybridType), size = 1) +
  geom_point(data = df_hybrid_trend, 
             aes(x = Year, y = Count, color = HybridType)) +
  # Custom fill scale for the corsage era
  scale_fill_manual(name = "", values = c("Cattleya Corsage Era" = "purple")) +
  labs(title = "Hybridization Trends Over Time", x = "Year", y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal() +
  # Make sure both legends show up
  guides(fill = guide_legend(override.aes = list(alpha = 0.2)))
```

```{r}
#Year vs Descendent #----------------------
ggplot(species_filtered, aes(x = species_filtered$Year, y = species_filtered$X..Descendants)) +

  labs(title = "Year vs. Number of Descendants",
       x = "Year",
       y = "Number of Descendants") +

#Descendent number by subgenera--------------------------------------------
ggplot(species_filtered, aes(x = species_filtered$Subgeneric.Ranks, y = species_filtered$X..Descendants)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  labs(title = "Number of Descendants by Subgeneric Rank",
       x = "Subgeneric Rank",
       y = "Number of Descendants") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
  theme_minimal()

#photo num by subgenera
ggplot(species_filtered, aes(x = species_filtered$Subgeneric.Ranks, y = species_filtered$X..Photos)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  labs(title = "Number of Photos by Subgeneric Rank",
       x = "Subgeneric Rank",
       y = "Number of Photos") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
  theme_minimal()

#number of descendents over time -- slightly misinformative as year isnt great for trends here
ggplot(species_filtered, aes(x = species_filtered$Year, y = species_filtered$X..Descendants)) +
  geom_line(stat = "summary", fun = "mean") +
  labs(title = "Trend of Number of Descendants Over Time",
       x = "Year",
       y = "Number of Descendants") +
  theme_minimal()

#subgeneric rank versus # descendents --> examine subgeneric ranks more closely
ggplot(species_filtered, aes(x = species_filtered$Subgeneric.Ranks, y = species_filtered$X..Descendants)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(title = "Box Plot of Number of Descendants by Subgeneric Rank",
       x = "Subgeneric Rank",
       y = "Number of Descendants") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
  theme_minimal()

#Pi chart of species descendents------------------------------------------

# Remove NA values in X..Descendants
species_filtered <- species_filtered %>% 
  filter(!is.na(X..Descendants))

# Calculate total number of descendants
total_descendants <- sum(species_filtered$X..Descendants)

# Calculate percentage of descendants for each species
species_filtered <- species_filtered %>% 
  mutate(Percentage = (X..Descendants / total_descendants) * 100)

# Sort species by percentage of descendants in descending order
species_filtered <- species_filtered %>% 
  arrange(desc(Percentage))

# Select top 10 species or fewer if there are less than 10
top_species <- head(species_filtered, 10)

# Combine remaining species into an "Other" category
other_percentage <- 100 - sum(top_species$Percentage)
other_data <- data.frame(Binomial = "Other", Percentage = other_percentage)

# Combine top species and other category
final_data <- bind_rows(top_species, other_data)

# Create a pie chart
ggplot(final_data, aes(x = "", y = Percentage, fill = Binomial)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 1) +
  coord_polar("y", start = 0) +
  theme_void() +
  labs(title = "Top Species by Percentage of Descendants",
       fill = "Species") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(hcl.colors(nrow(final_data) - 1, "Teal"), "grey")) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(round(Percentage, 1), "%")), 
            position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5), 
            color = "white", 
            size = 3.5)



```









```{r}
#phylogenetic tree plotting
library(ape)
library(ggtree)
library(tidyverse)

tree <- read.tree("../data/subtree-ottol-819061-Cattleya.tre")

tree$tip.label <- gsub("_", " ", tree$tip.label)  # Convert underscores to spaces if needed

tree_df <- fortify(tree)  # Convert tree to data frame

# Merge tree structure with species data
merged_data <- tree_df %>%
  left_join(species, by = c("label" = "Binomial"))

ggtree(tree) +
  geom_tiplab() + 
  geom_point2(aes(subset = !is.na(X..Descendants), color = X..Descendants, size = X..Photos),
              data = merged_data) +
  scale_color_gradient(low = "blue", high = "red") +
  theme_minimal()

##needs adjusted with different more accurate tree and smaller tree
```

```{r}
# Step 2: Reset row indices (CRUCIAL)

# Step 3: Extract last subgenus
df$LastSubgenus <- sapply(
  strsplit(df$Subgeneric.Ranks, "\n"),
  function(x) {
    x <- x[x != ""]           # remove empty strings
    if (length(x) == 0) return(NA_character_)  # handle missing
    tail(x, 1)                # get the last one
  }
)

# Step 4: Remove blank subgenus rows
df <- df[df$LastSubgenus != "", ]

# Step 5: Check again
stopifnot(length(df$LastSubgenus) == length(df$`X..Descendants`))

# Step 6: Run tapply
subgenus_hybrid_counts <- tapply(df$`X..Descendants`, df$LastSubgenus, sum, na.rm = TRUE)
```

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(caret)

# --- 1. Process Parentage Data --- #
hybrids_filtered <- hybrids_filtered %>%
  # Separate Parentage column into ParentA and ParentB with fill = "right"
  separate(Parentage, into = c("ParentA", "ParentB"), sep = " × ", remove = FALSE, fill = "right") %>%
  # Remove parentheses and their contents from ParentA and ParentB
  mutate(ParentA = str_remove(ParentA, " \\([^)]*\\)"),
         ParentB = str_remove(ParentB, " \\([^)]*\\)")) %>%
  # Filter out rows where either ParentA or ParentB is missing
  filter(!is.na(ParentA) & !is.na(ParentB))


# Compute parent popularity
parent_counts <- hybrids_filtered %>%
  select(ParentA, ParentB) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c("ParentA", "ParentB"), values_to = "Parent") %>%
  count(Parent, name = "Popularity")


# Merge popularity data
hybrids_filtered <- hybrids_filtered %>%
  left_join(parent_counts %>% rename(ParentA_Popularity = Popularity), by = c("ParentA" = "Parent")) %>%
  left_join(parent_counts %>% rename(ParentB_Popularity = Popularity), by = c("ParentB" = "Parent")) %>%
  mutate(
    ParentA_Popularity = replace_na(ParentA_Popularity, 1),
    ParentB_Popularity = replace_na(ParentB_Popularity, 1),
    Min_Parent_Popularity = pmin(ParentA_Popularity, ParentB_Popularity)
  ) %>%
  select(-ParentA_Popularity, -ParentB_Popularity)


# --- 2. Compute Species-Based Features --- #
species_contributions <- hybrids_filtered %>%
  select(Parentage, ParentA, ParentB) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c("ParentA", "ParentB"), values_to = "Species") %>%
  left_join(species, by = c("Species" = "Binomial")) %>%
  mutate(Is_Rare_Species = ifelse(X..Descendants < 10, TRUE, FALSE))

species_contributions <- species_contributions %>%
  group_by(Parentage, Species) %>%
  summarise(
    Total_Descendants = sum(X..Descendants, na.rm = TRUE),
    Species_Contribution = if_else(sum(Total_Descendants, na.rm = TRUE) == 0, NA_real_, Total_Descendants / sum(Total_Descendants, na.rm = TRUE)),
    Is_Rare_Species = any(Is_Rare_Species),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Fix Species1_Contribution to prevent -Inf issues
species_features <- species_contributions %>%
  left_join(hybrids_filtered %>% select(Parentage, ParentA, ParentB) %>% distinct(), by = "Parentage") %>%
  group_by(ParentA, ParentB) %>%
  summarise(
    Species1_Contribution = if_else(all(is.na(Species_Contribution)), NA_real_, max(Species_Contribution, na.rm = TRUE)),
    Species_Diversity = n_distinct(Species),
    Rare_Species_Contribution = sum(Species_Contribution[Is_Rare_Species], na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Species1_Contribution = if_else(Species1_Contribution == -Inf, NA_real_, Species1_Contribution)
  )

# Merge species features back into hybrids_filtered
hybrids_filtered <- hybrids_filtered %>%
  left_join(species_features, by = c("ParentA", "ParentB"))

# Ensure the column exists after merging
stopifnot("Species1_Contribution" %in% colnames(hybrids_filtered))

# --- 3. Assign Temporal Feature --- #
hybrids_filtered <- hybrids_filtered %>%
  mutate(Decade = floor(Year / 10) * 10)

# --- 4. Generate Unlikely hybrids_filtered --- #
set.seed(123)
all_parents <- unique(c(hybrids_filtered$ParentA, hybrids_filtered$ParentB))

candidate_hybrids_filtered <- expand.grid(ParentA = all_parents, ParentB = all_parents) %>%
  filter(ParentA != ParentB) %>%
  mutate(Parentage = paste(ParentA, ParentB, sep = " × ")) %>%
  left_join(species_features, by = c("ParentA", "ParentB")) %>%
  mutate(
    Min_Parent_Popularity = pmin(
      replace_na(parent_counts$Popularity[match(ParentA, parent_counts$Parent)], 1),
      replace_na(parent_counts$Popularity[match(ParentB, parent_counts$Parent)], 1)
    ),
    Hybrid_Type = sample(hybrids_filtered$HybridType, n(), replace = TRUE),
    Decade = sample(hybrids_filtered$Decade, n(), replace = TRUE)
  )

# Handle NA before ranking
candidate_hybrids_filtered <- candidate_hybrids_filtered %>%
  mutate(
    Species1_Contribution = replace_na(Species1_Contribution, 0),
    Species_Diversity = replace_na(Species_Diversity, 0),
    Rare_Species_Contribution = replace_na(Rare_Species_Contribution, 0)
  )

# Compute hybrid scores
candidate_hybrids_filtered <- candidate_hybrids_filtered %>%
  mutate(
    Score = rank(Min_Parent_Popularity) + rank(Species1_Contribution) +
            rank(Species_Diversity) + rank(Rare_Species_Contribution)
  )

negative_hybrids_filtered <- candidate_hybrids_filtered %>%
  arrange(Score) %>%
  slice_head(n = 500) %>%
  mutate(LikelyMade = 0)

# --- 5. Train the Predictive Model --- #
hybrids_filtered$LikelyMade <- 1

model_data <- bind_rows(
  hybrids_filtered %>%
    select(Parentage, Min_Parent_Popularity, Species1_Contribution, Species_Diversity, Rare_Species_Contribution, HybridType, Decade, LikelyMade),
  negative_hybrids_filtered %>%
    rename(HybridType = Hybrid_Type) %>%
    select(Parentage, Min_Parent_Popularity, Species1_Contribution, Species_Diversity, Rare_Species_Contribution, HybridType, Decade, LikelyMade)
)

# Ensure no missing values before training
model_data <- model_data %>%
  mutate(
    Min_Parent_Popularity = replace_na(Min_Parent_Popularity, 1),
    Species1_Contribution = replace_na(Species1_Contribution, 0),
    Species_Diversity = replace_na(Species_Diversity, 0),
    Rare_Species_Contribution = replace_na(Rare_Species_Contribution, 0)
  )

# Final check for NA/NaN/Inf
stopifnot(!any(is.na(model_data)))
summary(model_data)

# Split into training and test sets
set.seed(123)
train_index <- createDataPartition(model_data$LikelyMade, p = 0.8, list = FALSE)
train_data <- model_data[train_index, ]
test_data <- model_data[-train_index, ]

# Train the model
model <- glm(LikelyMade ~ Min_Parent_Popularity + Species1_Contribution + Species_Diversity + Rare_Species_Contribution + HybridType + Decade, 
             data = train_data, 
             family = binomial)

summary(model)

```


```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(caret)
library(vegan)  # For Shannon diversity calculation

# --- 1. Process Parentage Data --- #
hybrids_filtered <- hybrids_filtered %>%
  separate(Parentage, into = c("ParentA", "ParentB"), sep = " × ", remove = FALSE)

# Remove rows where ParentA or ParentB is missing
hybrids_filtered <- hybrids_filtered %>%
  filter(!is.na(ParentA) & !is.na(ParentB))

# Compute last hybridization year for each parent
last_hybridization <- hybrids_filtered %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(ParentA, ParentB), values_to = "Parent") %>%
  group_by(Parent) %>%
  summarise(Last_Hybrid_Year = max(Year, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# Merge to compute "Time since last hybridization"
hybrids_filtered <- hybrids_filtered %>%
  left_join(last_hybridization %>% rename(ParentA_LastHybrid = Last_Hybrid_Year), 
            by = c("ParentA" = "Parent")) %>%
  left_join(last_hybridization %>% rename(ParentB_LastHybrid = Last_Hybrid_Year), 
            by = c("ParentB" = "Parent")) %>%
  mutate(
    ParentA_LastHybrid = replace_na(ParentA_LastHybrid, min(Year, na.rm = TRUE)),
    ParentB_LastHybrid = replace_na(ParentB_LastHybrid, min(Year, na.rm = TRUE)),
    Time_Since_Last_Hybridization = Year - pmax(ParentA_LastHybrid, ParentB_LastHybrid)
  ) %>%
  select(-ParentA_LastHybrid, -ParentB_LastHybrid)

# --- 2. Compute Species-Based Features --- #
species_contributions <- hybrids_filtered %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c("ParentA", "ParentB"), values_to = "Species") %>%
  left_join(species, by = c("Species" = "Binomial")) %>%
  mutate(X..Descendants = replace_na(X..Descendants, 0),  # Ensure NA is replaced with 0
         Rarity_Score = 1 / (X..Descendants + 1))  # Higher score for rare species

# Summarize per hybrid
species_features <- species_contributions %>%
  group_by(Parentage) %>%
  summarise(
    Weighted_Rarity_Contribution = sum(Rarity_Score, na.rm = TRUE),
    Species_Diversity = ifelse(n_distinct(Species) > 1, diversity(table(Species), index = "shannon"), 0),
    Species1_Contribution = ifelse(sum(X..Descendants, na.rm = TRUE) > 0,
                                   max(X..Descendants, na.rm = TRUE) / sum(X..Descendants, na.rm = TRUE),
                                   0),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) 

# Ensure Species1_Contribution is present
species_features <- species_features %>%
  mutate(Species1_Contribution = replace_na(Species1_Contribution, 0))

# Normalize Species1_Contribution
species_features <- species_features %>%
  mutate(Species1_Contribution = (Species1_Contribution - min(Species1_Contribution, na.rm = TRUE)) /
                                   (max(Species1_Contribution, na.rm = TRUE) - min(Species1_Contribution, na.rm = TRUE)))

# Merge into hybrids_filtered
hybrids_filtered <- hybrids_filtered %>%
  left_join(species_features, by = "Parentage")

# --- 3. Convert Hybrid Type to Continuous Score --- #
hybrids_filtered <- hybrids_filtered %>%
  mutate(Hybrid_Complexity_Score = case_when(
    HybridType == "Primary" ~ 1,
    HybridType == "Complex" ~ 2,
    HybridType == "Highly Complex" ~ 3,
    TRUE ~ 2  # Default to 2 if unknown (assume it's a mid-level complexity)
  ))

# --- 4. Generate Unlikely Hybrids --- #
set.seed(123)
all_parents <- unique(c(hybrids_filtered$ParentA, hybrids_filtered$ParentB))

candidate_hybrids_filtered <- expand.grid(ParentA = all_parents, ParentB = all_parents) %>%
  filter(ParentA != ParentB) %>%
  mutate(Parentage = paste(ParentA, ParentB, sep = " × ")) %>%
  left_join(species_features, by = "Parentage")

# Ensure missing values are handled
candidate_hybrids_filtered <- candidate_hybrids_filtered %>%
  mutate(
    Time_Since_Last_Hybridization = sample(hybrids_filtered$Time_Since_Last_Hybridization, n(), replace = TRUE),
    Hybrid_Complexity_Score = sample(hybrids_filtered$Hybrid_Complexity_Score, n(), replace = TRUE),
    Species1_Contribution = replace_na(Species1_Contribution, 0),
    Species_Diversity = replace_na(Species_Diversity, 0),
    Weighted_Rarity_Contribution = replace_na(Weighted_Rarity_Contribution, 0)
  )

# Compute hybrid scores
candidate_hybrids_filtered <- candidate_hybrids_filtered %>%
  mutate(
    Score = rank(Time_Since_Last_Hybridization) + rank(Species1_Contribution) +
            rank(Species_Diversity) + rank(Weighted_Rarity_Contribution)
  )

negative_hybrids_filtered <- candidate_hybrids_filtered %>%
  arrange(Score) %>%
  slice_head(n = 500) %>%
  mutate(LikelyMade = 0)

# Ensure all necessary columns exist in negative_hybrids_filtered
negative_hybrids_filtered <- negative_hybrids_filtered %>%
  mutate(
    Time_Since_Last_Hybridization = replace_na(Time_Since_Last_Hybridization, 0),
    Hybrid_Complexity_Score = replace_na(Hybrid_Complexity_Score, 2),  # Default to 2
    Species1_Contribution = replace_na(Species1_Contribution, 0),
    Species_Diversity = replace_na(Species_Diversity, 0),
    Weighted_Rarity_Contribution = replace_na(Weighted_Rarity_Contribution, 0)
  )

# --- 5. Train the Predictive Model --- #
hybrids_filtered$LikelyMade <- 1

model_data <- bind_rows(
  hybrids_filtered %>%
    select(Parentage, Time_Since_Last_Hybridization, Species1_Contribution, 
           Species_Diversity, Weighted_Rarity_Contribution, Hybrid_Complexity_Score, LikelyMade),
  negative_hybrids_filtered %>%
    select(Parentage, Time_Since_Last_Hybridization, Species1_Contribution, 
           Species_Diversity, Weighted_Rarity_Contribution, Hybrid_Complexity_Score, LikelyMade)
)

# Check for missing values
stopifnot(!any(is.na(model_data)))

print("Data processing complete. Model data ready for training.")


```



```{r}

set.seed(42)
train_index <- createDataPartition(model_data$LikelyMade, p = 0.8, list = FALSE)
train_data <- model_data[train_index, ]
test_data <- model_data[-train_index, ]

train_data_balanced <- train_data %>%
  group_by(LikelyMade) %>%
  sample_n(min(table(train_data$LikelyMade))) %>%
  ungroup()

table(train_data$LikelyMade)

install.packages("ROSE")
library(ROSE)

train_data_balanced <- ROSE(LikelyMade ~ ., data = train_data, seed = 42)$data



train_data_balanced$LikelyMade <- as.factor(train_data_balanced$LikelyMade)
test_data$LikelyMade <- as.factor(test_data$LikelyMade)

rf_likely <- randomForest(
  LikelyMade ~ Time_Since_Last_Hybridization + Species1_Contribution + 
               Species_Diversity + Weighted_Rarity_Contribution + Hybrid_Complexity_Score,
  data = train_data_balanced,
  ntree = 500,
  mtry = 3,
  importance = TRUE
)


rf_unlikely <- randomForest(
  LikelyMade ~ Time_Since_Last_Hybridization + Species1_Contribution + 
               Species_Diversity + Weighted_Rarity_Contribution + Hybrid_Complexity_Score,
  data = train_data_balanced,
  ntree = 500,
  mtry = 3,
  importance = TRUE
)


pred_likely <- predict(rf_likely, test_data, type = "prob")[,2]  # Probability for likely hybrids
pred_unlikely <- predict(rf_unlikely, test_data, type = "prob")[,2]  # Probability for unlikely hybrids

final_predictions <- ifelse(pred_likely > pred_unlikely, 1, 0)


final_predictions

conf_matrix <- confusionMatrix(as.factor(final_predictions), as.factor(test_data$LikelyMade))
print(conf_matrix)
```
